record_type: Scientific erratum to prior HARNet preprocessing interpretation

corrects_prior_finding.claim_to_withdraw: The ordering of scaler.fit_transform before train/test interval selection was treated as evidence of fitting normalization parameters to future data.

retained_literal_fact: src/harnet/main.py line72 calls scaler.fit_transform(ts.to_numpy()) before constructing train/test index ranges in lines75-80.
reason_previous_inference_was_not_suppor: The scaler is a package-local class, not sklearn MinMaxScaler. Its fit_transform only calls transform. It does not estimate extrema or other parameters from the supplied series.

primary_evidence.finding: Factory constructs the local MinMaxScaler with cfg.scaler_min and cfg.scaler_max; Log, LogMinMax and None also select local classes.
MinMaxScaler stores constructor min/max; transform=(ts-min)/(max-min); fit_transform simply returns transform(ts).
LogMinMax, None and Log fit_transform methods also delegate directly to deterministic transforms without learning from supplied samples.
Default config sets scaler="MinMax", scaler_min=0.0, scaler_max=0.001.
SPX example selects scaler="MinMax" and does not override the default min/max values.

replacement_interpretation: The source call applies a transform across the loaded series; under the inspected fixed configuration it does not fit normalization extrema to that series. This ordering alone neither establishes leakage nor provides an integral audit of temporal validity.
not_established: How authors selected the fixed scaling constants before this commit
Full article protocol or reported results

independent_reproducibility_limitation.finding: The pinned public data header includes rv5 but not rv5_ss, whereas util.get_MAN_data selects rv5_ss at lines79/86. Default loading therefore cannot be assumed to run unchanged against the bundled CSV. No replacement variable or replication metrics are attributed to the original.
